Through a combination of software, network, platform, DevOps, data, delivery and security placements, you will develop the knowledge and practical experience needed to design, build, deploy, operate and secure modern digital systems. The starting salary for this role is £23,500 per annum. The Role Looking for a great start to your career in technology, earning and learning on a professionally accredited, award-winning scheme? We are recruiting the cyber, software, network, platform, DevOps, data and security professionals of the future on our nationally recognised, award-winning Degree Apprenticeship Programme. Our Cyber Degree Apprenticeship is broader than a traditional cybersecurity programme. It provides experience across the disciplines involved in designing, building, testing, deploying, operating and securing modern digital systems. This three-year programme combines Cyber Delivery (Engineering & Data) and Cyber Security, providing you with hands-on experience and a strong foundational skill set across engineering, data and security disciplines before you specialise in a chosen path. During Years 1 and 2, you will complete a series of placements across key areas, including: Core Foundational Skills System Development (Software, Network, Platform, DevOps and Test) Data & Analytics (AI/ML, Data Engineering and Visualisation) Security Risk & Governance and Audit & Assurance Operational Security, including exposure to Security Operations Centres (SOC), threat detection, vulnerability management and incident response Cyber Project Delivery, providing an understanding of how multidisciplinary teams plan, coordinate and deliver cyber and digital projects Exposure to how Architecture supports secure system design, engineering and technical decision-making In Year 3 you'll begin to specialise more in either Cyber Delivery or Cyber Security, having the opportunity to take on placements more focused on your chosen area and develop deeper expertise in preparation for a permanent role within the business. Throughout Your Apprenticeship, You Will: Balance your time between work and studying for a BSc (Hons) or BEng (Hons) in Cyber Security. Gain hands-on experience and practical skills in areas such as: Secure system and network design. Software, network, platform, DevOps and test engineering. Installing and configuring operating systems, firewalls and applications. Deploying and using secure Cloud environments such as AWS and Azure. Using DevOps practices and tooling to support secure software development, automation and deployment. Data analytics with Machine Learning and AI. Detecting and remediating cyberattacks. Security design and architecture, security testing and response investigations. Risk analysis, governance and compliance. Understanding how cyber and digital projects are planned and delivered. Engage in STEM outreach and community initiatives. During your Apprenticeship we encourage you to spend at least 3/4 days a week on site to integrate with your team and maximise your learning experience. Your work will support critical business areas throughout Leonardo and our customers in the UK government and private sector and will provide you with great learning opportunities in the field. At the same time, you will obtain the academic knowledge and qualifications necessary for your future career in a high-tech company through your course at one of our partner universities. You will be working within world-class facilities, in both office and lab environments and will have opportunities to travel to other Leonardo UK and customer sites, to meet with colleagues, customers, and suppliers. Beyond the programme there may be the opportunity for you to further your academic and vocational achievements based on your talents and capability and needs of the business. You would be expected to commit to the successful completion of all your academic modules and assignments in support of the Apprenticeship standard. What We’re Looking For This Apprenticeship assumes little prior cybersecurity experience and is NOT suitable for candidates who already have an engineering, software or computing degree. Qualification Requirements: 3 A-Levels (Grades A–C) One must be in Mathematics and another in Physics or an Engineering/Technology/IT related subject. OR BTEC Extended Diploma in Engineering (with maths bridging course). Plus: 5 GCSEs (Grades 9–4 / A*–C) including English, Maths, and a Science subject. We consider each application individually in consultation with our partnering university. Security Clearance At Leonardo, many of our roles are subject to security and export control restrictions set by UK Government Security requirements and customer obligations. As a result, and in line with the UK Government Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) requirements, all successful applicants will be asked to provide evidence of identity, eligibility to work in the UK, criminal record declaration information and employment and/or education history verification for the previous five years. For staff operating in more sensitive posts, there is an additional range of personnel security controls referred to as National Security Vetting (NSV). As part of this process, a range of factors may be considered, including an individual's background, travel history, nationality, previous nationalities held and other information relevant to the vetting assessment. To be eligible for National Security Vetting at SC level, applicants will generally be expected to have continuously resided in the UK for the previous five years. For DV clearance, this is typically ten years. In some circumstances, time spent overseas may be accepted, with additional overseas checks. Additional vetting requirements may apply upon appointment. For more information and guidance please visit: https://careers.uk.leonardo.com/gb/en/security-and-vetting Why join us At Leonardo, our people are at the heart of everything we do, key contributors in shaping innovation, advancing technology, and enhancing global safety. We offer a comprehensive, company-funded benefits package that supports your wellbeing, career development, and work–life balance. Whether you're looking to grow professionally, care for your health, or plan for the future, we’re here to help you thrive. Time to recharge: Enjoy generous leave with the opportunity to accrue up to 12 additional flexi-days each year. Secure your future: Benefit from our award-winning pension scheme with up to 15% employer contribution. Your wellbeing matters: Free access to mental health support, financial advice, and employee-led networks championing inclusion and diversity. Rewarding performance: All employees are eligible for our bonus scheme. Join in our success: Our annual Employee Stock Ownership Plan provides you the opportunity to own shares in Leonardo. Tailored perks: Spend up to £500 annually on flexible benefits including private healthcare, dental, family cover, tech & lifestyle discounts, gym memberships and more. For a full list of our company benefits please visit: https://careers.uk.leonardo.com/gb/en/company-benefits We are committed to building an inclusive, accessible, and welcoming workplace. We believe that a diverse workforce sparks creativity, drives innovation, and leads to better outcomes for our people, communities and our customers. If you have any accessibility requirements to support you during the recruitment process, just let us know. Be part of something extraordinary - apply now! review_candidates.description: Employment Executive Director / President Organization Code for Science & Society (CS&S) Type Full-Time Salary $225,000 to $250,000 / Yearly Four-day Week No About Code For Science & Society Code for Science & Society (CS&S) is a nonprofit, fiscal sponsorship organization working to advance the power of data to improve the social and economic lives of all people. CS&S focuses on supporting the social and organizational infrastructure that allows data, research, and technology to improve lives through its best-in-class Fiscal Sponsorship Program. In practice, the organization provides the operational backbone public interest technology projects need to thrive. Sponsored projects across community-centered research and technology development receive comprehensive financial and operational support – from back-office infrastructure to strategic guidance on governance, organizational project development, and sustainability – so project leaders can focus on their mission rather than the administration of running a nonprofit. CS&S is home to 20 fiscally sponsored projects spanning open data, open source software, open scholarship, and research infrastructure. THE CURRENT MOMENT CS&S is experiencing a moment of transition and opportunity. The departure of a long-tenured leader positions CS&S for a new chapter of strategic leadership and impact. The current cultural and political climate has brought heightened visibility, vulnerability, and urgency to the advancement of public interest technology. At the same time, the funding landscape is shifting. Internally, CS&S is experiencing the need for renewed strategic clarity, and the next Executive Director / President (Executive Director) will guide the organization to become an even more visible and catalytic force, building on its role as fiscal sponsor and leaning into the opportunity to serve as a best-in-class model of critical infrastructure support. This leadership transition creates a rare and exciting opportunity to deepen CS&S’ impact, strengthen resource development, evolve strategic vision, and reaffirm CS&S as a powerful champion for public interest technology. THE OPPORTUNITY Role CS&S seeks a visionary, strategic leader with strong executive presence, fundraising acumen, and a deep understanding of fiscal sponsorship excellence. The successful candidate will have a demonstrated commitment to the success of the public interest technology and open-source communities and possess a combination of strategic sophistication and results orientation, balancing external engagement with internal capacity building. Areas for impact in this role include: Resource Development. Ensuring CS&S’ long-term financial stability and capacity for growth will be a central leadership priority. The Executive Director will take a holistic approach to resource development, expanding both the fundraising strength and the business development capacity of CS&S and its fiscal projects. They will diversify revenue streams, cultivate relationships with new and existing institutional and philanthropic funders and new donor communities, and identify and pursue innovative revenue and partnership opportunities. Through strategic leadership, relationship building, an entrepreneurial mindset, and a sophisticated understanding of today’s funding landscape, they will diversify and grow the resources that fuel CS&S’ impact. Financial Strategy. The Executive Director will bring strategic insight to guide sound decision‑making and deepen organizational understanding of financial risks and opportunities within the fiscal sponsorship model. They will oversee financial health and asset management, sustain and grow reserves, and guide thoughtful choices about resource allocation that advance CS&S’ mission. Organizational Strategy. The Executive Director will bring a current understanding of fiscal sponsorship models and the fiscal sponsor field to effectively navigate the broader nonprofit infrastructure environment. They will monitor changing landscapes, trends, and developments to ensure that CS&S is selecting objectives and deploying resources as effectively as possible to achieve their goals. The Executive Director will clarify CS&S’ theory of change and define short- and long-term organizational strategy and scope, and as a result, CS&S’ external positioning to strengthen the organization’s external and fundraising profile. Organizational Leadership. The Executive Director will serve as the visible leader of CS&S, guiding the organization internally and representing it externally. They will report to the Board of Directors, lead a core team staff of 9, and manage 2 direct reports. They will be an effective leader of teams, cultivating talent, fostering trust, and inspiring a positive internal culture grounded in collaboration, transparency, and service excellence for fiscal sponsorship partners. They will actively listen to staff needs and aspirations and cultivate an environment in which individuals and teams can thrive. They will also support fiscally sponsored projects individually and collectively, clarify organizational scope, and build alignment across projects. Externally, the Executive Director will serve as a trusted partner to funders and the field, contribute to thought leadership to advance best practices, and contribute to innovations that strengthen critical nonprofit infrastructure. Fiscal Sponsorship Strategies. The Executive Director will serve as a vocal advocate and champion for CS&S’ projects with funders and across funder communities. They will strengthen funders’ understanding of the mission, vision, and values of projects; invite innovative and collaborative funding opportunities; and elevate CS&S as a valuable infrastructure model within a changing funding landscape. The Executive Director will also serve as a thought partner and resource to fiscally sponsored partners through reliable, forward-thinking, and best-in-class operational support to enable projects to execute their missions and impacts in the field. Governance and Organizational Structure. The Executive Director will develop and maintain a relationship with the Board of Directors that is defined by trust, respect, transparency, and clear communication. They will partner with the Board to strengthen governance, clarify priorities, and promote alignment. They will grow the Board through strategic recruitment and work with the Board as it continues to develop as a strategic governing body that is fully engaged in governance, long-term planning, and effective oversight to position CS&S for even greater impact. Desired Qualifications CS&S values and will evaluate the totality of a candidate’s experience, including both lived and professional experience. The ideal candidate will possess many of the attributes above and many of the following professional abilities and experiences. Executive and Strategic Leadership At least 10+ years of senior or executive leadership in fiscal sponsorship, nonprofit leadership, philanthropy, and/or a related sector. Experience navigating complex organizational environments, complex nonprofit infrastructure, leading change with steadiness, and making disciplined and strategic decisions. Experience providing leadership and being a collaboration-oriented leader for the development and execution of strategic vision in a changing funding and political landscape. Fundraising and Resource Development Proven track record of cultivating, soliciting, and stewarding major donors and securing major gifts on behalf of an organization and specific organizational projects by building strong, trustbased relationships grounded in transparency, authenticity, and humility. Experience co-designing long-term fundraising strategies, collaborative fundraising strategies, diversifying funding streams, and strengthening a culture of giving with project leads. Demonstrated excellence in fundraising-focused communication with a proven ability to inspire confidence as a relationship builder, persuasive public speaker, and skilled writer addressing diverse funder audiences. Organizational and People Leadership People-centered leader with effective skills in leading teams and building service-oriented, high performing organizational cultures. Solutions-oriented mindset with skills in delegation, communication, and creating conditions for staff to thrive individually and collectively. Experience partnering with a Board of Directors to strengthen governance and strategic alignment. Mission and Values Alignment Demonstrated commitment to the mission and vision of public interest technology, open source, open data, open tech, and open research communities. Authentic understanding of the unique operational and infrastructure needs of early-stage, maturing, and mature nonprofit organizations. Financial & Operational Acumen Strong financial literacy, including experience managing budgets, assessing risk, and guiding organizational sustainability. Ability to align resources with strategic priorities and ensure operational systems support an evolving institution. Compensation And Benefits Code for Science & Society offers a competitive annual salary within the range of $225,000 – $250,000 for the Executive Director position, complemented by a comprehensive benefits package that includes eligibility for medical, dental, and vision coverage, life insurance, and a 401(k) plan with a 4% employer match. CS&S also offers unlimited paid time off (PTO) and company-paid holidays to support employee well-being and time away from work. Code for Science & Society is a remote-first organization, with team members and contractors located around the world. CS&S fosters a flexible, inclusive, and collaborative work environment where leaders are empowered to drive meaningful impact while maintaining work-life balance. This search is being led by Ellen LaPointe and Sharon Gertsman of the national talent search firm NPAG. If you are excited by this opportunity and believe the role is a strong match to your skills and experiences, we invite your application, resume, and cover letter outlining your interest and qualifications via the portal on NPAG’s website. We consider all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, marital status, or any other status protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.
